gloss: to dress (fish); to handle skillfully; to sell off

definitions.gloss: to dress (fish or game); to fillet; to butcher
definitions.explanation: To cut up a fish, chicken, or other animal into edible parts — removing scales, bones, or organs. A standard kitchen / fishmonger skill.

definitions.gloss: to handle skillfully; to manage; to deal with
definitions.explanation: To deal smoothly with a large number of things — work, customers, tasks, traffic — without getting overwhelmed. Implies competence and speed.

examples.japanese: {鶏肉|とりにく}を{捌|さば}くのは{初|はじ}めてだ。
examples.english: It's my first time dressing a chicken.

examples.japanese: {板前|いたまえ}さんが{目|め}の{前|まえ}で{大|おお}きなマグロを{捌|さば}いてくれた。
examples.english: The chef dressed a large tuna right in front of us.

examples.japanese: お{客|きゃく}さんをうまく{捌|さば}く。
{仕事|しごと}が{多|おお}くてとても{捌|さば}ききれない。
examples.english: There's so much work I can't possibly handle it all.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{忙|いそが}しい{時間帯|じかんたい}でも{注文|ちゅうもん}を{次々|つぎつぎ}と{捌|さば}いていく。
examples.english: Even during busy hours, he handles one order after another.

notes:
Transitive godan verb. Both senses share the core idea of 'cutting through and handling efficiently'. Note that {裁|さば}く (judge a case) and {砂漠|さばく} (desert) are unrelated homophones.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {魚|さかな}を{捌|さば}く: to dress / fillet a fish
- {仕事|しごと}を{捌|さば}く: to power through work
- {在庫|ざいこ}を{捌|さば}く: to sell off inventory
- {交通|こうつう}を{捌|さば}く: (police, etc.) to manage traffic flow

ASPECT (ている):
{捌|さば}いている often describes someone in the middle of efficiently handling work or customers, emphasizing the continuous, smooth flow of activity.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {処理|しょり}する: to process; to handle — more formal/neutral; lacks the 'skillful flow' nuance of {捌|さば}く
- {対応|たいおう}する: to deal with — used for responding to situations / requests, more passive feel

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {捌|さば}いていませんでした
